# SSH-012: Host keys are strong and private

- **Group:** SSH
- **Severity when it fails:** moderate
- **Root:** not needed

## Why it matters

A host private key readable by other users lets them impersonate the server to every client. DSA host keys are obsolete and RSA keys under 3072 bits are below current guidance. Only the metadata of the private key is read, never its contents.

## Verify by hand

```sh
ls -l /etc/ssh/ssh_host_*; for f in /etc/ssh/ssh_host_*_key.pub; do ssh-keygen -lf "$f"; done
```

## How to fix it

chmod 600 the private keys and chown them to root; remove DSA keys and regenerate a small RSA key with ssh-keygen -t rsa -b 4096 -f /etc/ssh/ssh_host_rsa_key.

## What a fix can break

Regenerating a host key changes the server fingerprint: clients see a host key warning until known_hosts is updated.

Run `stackward explain SSH-012` for the same text in your terminal. [All checks](index.md).
